Live from NPR News, I'm Dale Willman.
President Trump says he's rejecting a short-term plan offered by Iran to reopen the Strait
of Hormuz in seven days.
The proposed plan would also have temporarily ended hostilities in order to restart cease-fire
talks with the U.S.
And Pierre's Emily Feng has more on the story.
Iran had proposed the plan this week at the United Nations General Assembly meetings in
New York, a plan very similar to a memorandum of understanding that the two countries agreed
upon back in June.
And Iran's president told CBS News he'd allow UN nuclear inspectors into Iran if there
were a long-term cease-fire deal with the U.S.
But Trump wrote on True Social Saturday morning, "Iran cannot have a nuclear weapon," and
then told reporters before departing for Tennessee that the plan was "not acceptable."
Trump claimed Iran was negotiating out of a position of weakness and said they were "dying."
Emily Feng and Pierre News, Washington.
In Hawaii, Hurricane Nolo is still moving close to that island chain, but as Hawaii
Public Radio's Bill Dorman reports, the effects are turning out to be less catastrophic than
anticipated.
The National Hurricane Center still expects Nolo to strengthen to a major hurricane on
Sunday and peak in intensity on Monday, but its impact on the islands is now projected
to be less than originally feared.
Tropical storm force winds are howling through parts of Hawaii Island and may develop at
high altitudes on Maui, but forecasts of wind speeds and rainfall have declined.
The storm center is moving west and expected to pick up speed as it moves further away
from the island chain.
Still, the National Weather Service says strong and gusty winds are possible for all the Hawaiian
Islands this weekend.
For NPR News, I'm Bill Dorman in Honolulu.
The Hawaiian island chain is still recovering from two previous storms, Hurricane Lala and
Lowell.
Control of the House is on the line in November with both parties fighting over a relatively
small number of competitive districts.
One of those battles runs through Allentown, Pennsylvania, which is a majority Latino city,
and Pierre's Barbara Sprunt has our reports.
Here in Allentown, worries about the economy and cost of living reign supreme.
Former Gonzales Rosati sees the toll it takes as she runs a daycare.
Regardless of your political party or your ethnicity, we're all feeling the same things.
It's gotten to the point where there's almost, or we're gearing towards two class of people,
the filthy rich or the dirt poor.
We're squeezing out the middle class.
Republicans made inroads with Latino voters in the 24 cycle, something they're trying
to replicate come November.
Barbara Sprunt and Pierre News, Allentown, Pennsylvania.
Now as Democrats, meanwhile, are preparing a widespread agenda if their party takes back
control in this November's elections, they're planning investigations of President Trump,
his administration, his children, and alleged corporate wrongdoing.
You're listening to NPR News.
Officials in Greece say six bodies have been recovered from the rubble of a collapsed building
in Athens near the Acropolis.
The U.S. ambassador to Greece says four of the victims were Americans.
The building collapsed Friday morning following the explosion.
Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, and TikTok are all refusing to run advertisements for an
upcoming documentary on billionaire Elon Musk.
As NPR's Bobby Allen reports, Musk has threatened to sue over the nearly four-hour film, calling
it a hit job.
The documentary is called Musk.
It's by Oscar-winning director Alex Gibney, and it's set for release next month.
The film is a scathing look at the tech mogul's life from his childhood in South Africa, his
rise in Silicon Valley, including his takeover of the site formerly known as Twitter, along
with his time in the White House.
Gibney asks, "How did one man become so powerful?"
It's a message deemed too political by meta, YouTube, and TikTok, all of which have refused
to carry ads about the film.
That's according to a person close to the production who wasn't authorized to speak
publicly.
Earlier this month, lawyers for Musk threatened to file a defamation lawsuit over the film.
Musk would not sit for an interview with Gibney.
Instead, he used an AI-generated avatar of Musk as a stand-in.
Bobbie Allen, NPR News.
It was a big win for Florida Saturday as the No. 21 ranked gator is pounded No. 4 Ole Miss
52-28.
No. 1 Texas escaped with a win, holding off No. 14 Tennessee and Knoxville 20-17.
Jeremiah Smith tied an Ohio State record with four touchdowns as the Buckeyes beat Illinois
42-19.
No. 2 Georgia and No. 3 Notre Dame easily won their games, while No. 5 Indiana struggled
to beat Northwestern 29-23.
And cocaine beat Rio Grande Red Storm 53-0.
